architecture.approach: Port the quota-ledger crate from feature/m3-substrate as prior art and adapt it to the current workspace: one library crate at crates/quota-ledger, feature-gated with default = [] and an additive postgres feature. The core is a set of value types (identity, metric, window, budget, policy, key, reservation, usage), a single QuotaError enum, and an async QuotaStore trait with four operations. MemoryQuotaStore is the reference implementation and the deterministic test seam. The postgres feature adds a second QuotaStore implementation over a caller-supplied connection, whose atomicity comes from a conditional UPDATE rather than a lock held in the library. The crate depends on platform-core for tenant and provider identity so a tenant is one tenant across the stack, and never becomes a database or an HTTP client.

dataModel.flowDescription: A caller derives a QuotaKey from the authenticated tenant and the provider, then reserves before the outbound call. reserve checks capacity and records a hold atomically, returning a Reservation or a typed QuotaExceeded. On success the caller commits, which consumes the hold exactly once; on a definite provider rejection the caller releases it, returning the held amount to the budget. usage reports limit, consumed, held, and the next reset. In the Postgres backend the claim is a single conditional UPDATE whose WHERE clause includes the remaining-capacity predicate, so the database serializes concurrent claims and two pods cannot both take the final unit. Instrumentation events are emitted for reserved, denied, committed, and released.

securityConsiderations.description: Every store operation is keyed by the tenant in the QuotaKey, so no read or write can cross a tenant boundary.
Every Postgres statement is parameterized; caller values never reach SQL text, which keeps the ledger clear of injection.
Caller-supplied windows, metrics, and keys are validated and an invalid window produces a typed error rather than a guessed default.
The crate reads no credentials from the environment or a file; the caller supplies the connection, and a Postgres connection must use TLS.

performanceConsiderations.strategy: The reserve path is a single conditional statement rather than a read-then-write pair, which removes both a round trip and the lost-update race.
The memory backend uses interior sharding by key so the reference implementation does not serialize unrelated budgets during tests.

resolution.reason: The sqlx facade was dropped in T5.1: it declares sqlx-mysql and sqlx-sqlite as optional dependencies on itself, so Cargo resolved them into Cargo.lock regardless of features and dragged rsa (RUSTSEC-2023-0071) into the audit of a build that never compiled it. Replaced by the two driver crates below, so the facade is no longer a dependency.

risks.description: The postgres backend is the hardest part to verify without a live database, so a defect in the atomic claim may pass review.
risks.mitigation: AC-013 asserts the concurrency invariant directly, and the prior art ships a Postgres test harness to adapt.
